engagement_background.objective: Advantia Health hired Treya Partners to identify and capture cost-savings across major spend categories, strengthen procurement discipline, and thereby increase EBITDA/enterprise value for its PE sponsors.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Treya will run savings-creation efforts in 10 spend categories representing about $19 M in annual spend (e.g., employee benefits, medical devices & supplies, billing/RCM, telecom, IT, office supplies). Work includes competitive bids, incumbent negotiations, GPO leverage, and a procurement process/controls review; Employee Benefits is an optional later work-stream and some categories may be dropped if found non-addressable.
constraints_challenges: Limited strategic procurement resources and focus within Advantia prior to the engagement
Purchasing split between Mid-Atlantic and Heartland business units, leading to supplier fragmentation and decentralized decision making
Incomplete line-item and usage data; Treya must obtain additional data directly from key suppliers
Multiple AP and P-card systems with inconsistent vendor naming conventions complicate spend visibility
Aggressive six-month timeline (Benefits stream to follow) tied to PE value-creation goals
Need to manage sensitivities around long-standing incumbent supplier relationships while pursuing savings

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP and P-card transaction data for Oct-2020 through Sep-2021 from two systems were available; limited contract files and minimal item-level usage data.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Spend scattered across multiple systems, supplier names not standardized, and notable gaps in historical usage data requiring supplier outreach.
